read_first: world runtime receipt for each process being advanced
only due or causally awakened process coverage/owners
write_order: determine every boundary, owner-local deadline and causal wake-up crossed before the target time
settle awakened owners and every supported successor action in chronological order
persist authoritative domain-owner effects before declaring process settlement
write or replace the process latest semantic receipt in state/runtime.json with the actual outcome and coverage used
advance that process frontier cursor only to the exact reviewed_through value proven by its receipt
after every required continuous process is closed, advance the runtime/global frontier to the target
end with no overdue boundary, owner-local deadline, causal wake-up or unreceipted continuous process
invariants: Aggregate coverage may batch stable descendants but never improve their outcomes.
A process frontier timestamp is orchestration state, not evidence that its covered owners were reviewed; the matching runtime receipt supplies that evidence.
A no_op receipt requires an actual semantic review with a causal reason; silently skipping an owner or leaving a file untouched is not a no-op.
Owner-local schedules and causal wake-ups override a slower aggregate baseline such as monthly review.
Material autonomous actions are instantiated and persisted in their domain authority before successor resolution continues.
